description: Fires when the agent is about to end its turn. Reads the assistant's own just-written reply from the turn's transcript and checks it against the banned-word dictionary at ~/.claude/DICT.json (the same file `tg` enforces for outgoing Telegram messages) — closing the gap where that enforcement had zero effect on text typed directly into the Claude Code chat UI. Blocks (exit 10) on a real hit, quoting the matched text, the violated rule id, its reason, and the correct replacement. A rule marked only_if_cyrillic applies only when the whole current-turn text contains Cyrillic, judged once over the whole turn (not per-rule), so plain English text is never affected by a Russian-only rule. Re-checks and blocks on every Stop with a real violation (no cooldown) but caps consecutive violating Stops per session (default 3, CHAT_DICT_GATE_LOOP_GUARD_CAP) so a model that cannot converge on clean wording cannot wedge the session forever — crossing the cap allows anyway under its own decision string. Priority 10 is deliberate and load-bearing, not cosmetic: agents-hooks/v1 runs stop-point hooks in ascending (priority, id) order and the first BLOCK short-circuits the rest for that Stop event, so this hook must sort ahead of stop-completion-selfcheck (priority 50, the only other stop hook that can emit exit 10 today) or a banned-word violation could be masked by that hook's own block on the same Stop event. Fails OPEN (on_error=open) on every dictionary lifecycle problem too, not just process crashes: a missing default dictionary silently disables the gate, but a missing explicit override, malformed JSON, or an uncompilable rule regex allows the stop with a stderr warning rather than trapping the user's turn over a config typo — a deliberate divergence from tg-cli's fail-closed posture, justified in the README.
